title: Per-variant working-set bucketing and prefetch policy for extended-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: For Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants running at extended context lengths (32k-64k tokens), our current KV residency and continuous-batching heuristics either over-allocate GPU memory or cause unnecessary mid-inference spills. This increases p99 latency and unit-cost for steady workloads that maintain long live prefixes (e.g., conversation histories, code sessions).

Goal: Implement per-variant 'working-set bucketing' (a compact summary of active KV slices per layer and token-range) plus a predictive prefetch/decay policy that cooperates with continuous batching so we maintain low latency while minimizing allocated GPU footprint across model variants and sequence distributions.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design and implement an adaptive per-variant working-set bucketer that classifies active KV ranges into hot/warm/cold buckets per-layer and per-variant.
- Implement a prefetch policy tied to batch composition: when a request is admitted, estimate which buckets will be used in the next N tokens and prefetch into GPU memory proactively.
- Add a decay eviction schedule for warm/cold buckets that is latency-aware (do not evict buckets that would cause p95 increase > target).
- Metricized canary rollout and A/B bench harness across Llama-2-70B, Mistral-1.4, and Qwen-7B-Chat variants at 32k/64k contexts.
- Integration with runtime continuous batching to ensure prefetch doesn't starve throughput (safety limits + async prefetch).

Why this is different: Existing work focused on static KV slicing and slot-pinning. This ticket introduces a time-series working-set view with explicit prefetch windows and decay schedules that adapt to model behavior and request mix, reducing transient spikes in allocation and lowering average committed memory per GPU without changing kernel selection.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation merged and feature-flagged behind runtime.working_set_bucketing
Bench results show >= 15% median GPU-committed-memory reduction for mixed steady conversational workloads at 32k and >= 18% at 64k for at least two model variants
p95 latency regression <= 5% relative to baseline in steady-state (no colder-than-expected user patterns)
No increased OOM incidence on dedicated pools during canary (0 OOMs over 24h canary across 10 nodes)
Operational dashboards (Grafana) surface per-variant bucket occupancy and prefetch hit-rate
Documentation and rollout runbook updated (Confluence doc + runbook steps)
comments: 2026-01-29 — Triage: Added after memory heatmap spike investigation; flagged as P1 due to customer reports of increased costs for long-chat products.
2026-02-05 — Architecture sketch completed. Decided on 3-bucket model (hot/warm/cold) with per-layer occupancy counters and an exponential decay window. Link to design doc added.

2026-02-18 — Prototype: Implemented bucket estimator in the runtime sim harness. Early microbench shows 12% committed memory savings on Mistral-1.4 at 32k with naive prefetch window. CPU overhead acceptable (<2% throughput impact).

2026-02-23 — Integrated prefetch scheduler with continuous-batching admission controller; added async eviction queue to prevent blocking token generation. Observed 3% p95 latency improvement for sessions with stable prefixes.
2026-03-01 — Bench iteration: Qwen-7B shows 20% savings on median memory but a 6% p95 latency regression under bursty arrival patterns. Added conservative prefetch cap per-request to mitigate.

2026-03-05 — Design review with PM/Design/Runtime team. Feedback: expose prefetch aggressiveness as a per-project policy in Console and surface bucket signals in per-route tracing. Action: add feature flag and Console controllable knob.
2026-03-08 — PR opened: runtime/pull/5580 (bucket metadata, admission integration, metrics). Requesting engineering review and perf stamp.
2026-03-10 — Blocker: need guidance from infra on GPU memory accounting changes for committed vs resident memory metrics. Pinged infra team (ENG-198765) for dependency resolution.
implementation_notes: Representation: store per-layer bucket bitmaps compressed (run-length encoding) to bound memory overhead for metadata
Prefetch window heuristics: start with lookahead=4 tokens for generative flows and adaptive lookahead for chat-style turns based on recent turn lengths
Safety: implement budgeted async prefetch (max prefetch bytes per request) and per-GPU token-budget guardrails
Telemetry: emit bucket_hit, bucket_miss, prefetch_bytes, bucket_evictions, and per-variant occupancy_percent metrics
Rollout: staged canary by model family -> region -> dedicated pool -> global, with automatic rollback on increased OOM or >10% p95 latency regression
